papers.title: UCO: A Multi-Turn Interactive Reinforcement Learning Method for Adaptive Teaching with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Shouang Wei, Min Zhang, Xin Lin, Bo Jiang, Kun Kuang, Jingyuan Chen, Zhongxiang Dai
papers.summary: UCO is a multi-turn interactive RL method for adaptive teaching with two rewards. A Progress Reward checks whether students truly move from confusion to comprehension rather than echoing answers the teacher gave them. A Scaffold Reward identifies each student's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and keeps teaching within it. The method is compared with 11 baselines on BigMath and MathTutorBench.
key_findings: Earlier RL tutors judged teaching only by whether the student produced a correct output. They could not tell genuine understanding from echoing the teacher's answer, and could not track evolving cognitive states in real time.
UCO introduces two rewards. A Progress Reward captures the move from confusion to comprehension. A Scaffold Reward identifies each student's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD).
Against 11 baselines on BigMath and MathTutorBench, UCO outperforms all models of the same scale and is comparable to advanced closed-source models.
practices: Mastery checks should require the learner to apply the concept to a new case in their own words. Echoing the tutor's answer does not count as mastery.
Track a per-concept ZPD and adapt the level of support to it.
papers.verify_note: Verified via the arXiv API (v4). Acceptance at the EMNLP 2026 main conference is confirmed in the arXiv comment. The first arXiv version dates from 2025. Added the reward design and benchmark details.

papers.title: Curiosity as Linguistic Intervention: Using LLM Tutoring Dialogues to Influence Exploratory Learning Behavior
papers.authors: Gevindu Ganganath, Pasindu Bolonghege, Qianru Lyu, Pradeep Varakantham, Thivya Kandappu
papers.summary: CURIOBOT turns Berlyne's collative variables (novelty, complexity, conflict, uncertainty) into adaptive linguistic interventions for conversational tutoring. It is tested on 270 tutoring conversations across model families, domains and topic complexity levels. The authors also introduce a learner-centred evaluation covering exploratory questioning, conversational agency, productive struggle and observable curiosity.
key_findings: CURIOBOT turns Berlyne's collative variables (novelty, complexity, conflict, uncertainty) into adaptive linguistic interventions for tutoring.
Across 270 tutoring conversations, curiosity-oriented interventions consistently increased exploratory learner behaviour, producing up to 2.4x more conversational turns under fixed time budgets.
Learner-side gains held even when tutor-side instructional quality stayed the same. This suggests curiosity works as a partly independent interaction-level mechanism.
practices: Open a concept with a curiosity hook built on novelty, conflict or uncertainty, for example a paradox the learner has to resolve.
Measure learner-side engagement (exploratory questions, agency, productive struggle), not only tutor-side quality.

papers.title: Socrates went Nuclear: Comparing Interaction Strategies for AI systems in a Learning Context using Brain Sensing
papers.authors: Alexandre Clin Deffarges, Nataliya Kosmyna, Pattie Maes
papers.venue: HAI '26 (14th Int. Conf. on Human-Agent Interaction), to appear; arXiv
papers.summary: Fifty participants learned nuclear safety protocols, a domain with essentially no prior knowledge, under one of three conditions: an unrestricted chatbot, a Socratic mode that gave hints but no final answers, and a non-conversational tutor that adapted difficulty from EEG-derived engagement (Muse headband). Learning was measured with a pre-test and an immediate post-test.
key_findings: The study compared an unrestricted chatbot, a Socratic hint-only bot and an EEG-adaptive, non-conversational tutor. Fifty participants learned nuclear safety protocols, a topic chosen so that no one had prior knowledge.
The unrestricted chatbot produced higher learning gains than both constrained modes (p < .03, d > 0.80). The adaptive condition produced significantly higher EEG engagement (p = .018).
Most unrestricted-mode users retrieved answers directly. Socratic-mode users first tried to reason through the hints, then progressively disengaged.
The authors suggest the unrestricted chatbot's advantage reflects the immediate post-test rather than deeper learning.
practices: For factual content the learner cannot yet know, avoid pure Socratic questioning and allow short explanations when knowledge is missing.
Watch for disengagement during Socratic hinting and adapt the strategy.
Evaluate with delayed or transfer measures, not only an immediate post-test.
papers.verify_note: Verified via the arXiv API. The HAI'26 'to appear' status is confirmed in the arXiv comment. Added the study design details. The specific disengagement signals in the original practice (shrinking replies, runs of 'I don't know') are not in the abstract and were generalized.
